reasoning_summary: Three independent blockers prevent build_now: the total score of 5.8 falls below the 6.5 build threshold, operational_autonomy (6) misses its floor of 7 due to per-repo onboarding complexity, and buildability_with_ai (5) misses its floor of 6 because shipping requires non-trivial CI/CD integration (GitHub App, webhook auth, repo permissions) that the factory cannot accomplish with standard prompt-plus-landing-page tooling alone. The cost_to_gain_ratio of 6.42 also far exceeds the 0.6 kill threshold, and expected_gain_90d is negative (-$142), signaling that even optimistic unit economics do not justify commitment today. However, the pain is real, frequent, and structurally tied to a growing trend (agentic coding adoption), and the buyer segment (engineering teams already paying for AI coding tools) is credible — so an outright kill is premature. The right next step is a validation probe: confirm whether a simpler product form (e.g., a standalone CLI or pre-commit hook rather than a full SaaS GitHub App) could raise buildability and autonomy scores above their floors, and run a lightweight responsiveness test against 50 engineering leads to see if anyone would pay for test-governance tooling specifically.
